findings.problem: In everyday English, a bare "phone" usually means a mobile phone, and in Latin America that is "el celular", so a learner could fairly answer "el celular" instead of "el teléfono".

back.example: Will you give me your phone number?

note: Another way to fix it is to keep en as "phone" and add the hint "the general word, not specifically a mobile (that's celular)".
